name: Alloy Robotics
description: Alloy connects Claude to your organization's robot mission and Mesh Storage data. Search missions and images, inspect summaries, reports, scenarios, devices, and data-lake tables, run read-only analysis, create reports and artifacts, manage report automations, and perform approved device or edge-configuration actions.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Alloy Robotics to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Alloy Robotics to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://aus.usealloy.ai/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Alloy Robotics MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Alloy Robotics lists 43 MCP tools, including approve_device, browse_mesh_storage, create_data_artifact, create_dev_device_key, create_inline_artifact, create_report, create_triggered_prompt, describe_mesh_table, find_similar_images, get_binary_setup, get_docker_setup, and get_edge_config.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Alloy Robotics?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Alloy Robotics in data-analytics on the Manufact MCP catalog include Epicure, Newsflash, Point Topic, Pricing Optimizer AI, and StatCite.

_published_faq.name: Does Alloy Robotics MCP require authentication?

acceptedAnswer.text: Alloy Robotics requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
Alloy Robotics is developed by Alloy Robotics. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
